mainTopic: Whether a mother inherits from her son, and the new משנה on the order of heirs, where each heir's descendants stand in his place.
overview: רבי יהודה בן שמעון holds, based on the word 'מטות', that a mother inherits from her son. רבי יוחנן objects from our משנה, which says a mother passes inheritance to her son but does not inherit from him. רבי יהודה בן שמעון answers only that he does not know who taught that משנה. The גמרא shows why he could not say it follows רבי זכריה בן הקצב: the same משנה puts a sister's sons before her daughters, but רבי זכריה treats sons and daughters equally in a mother's property. The גמרא then asks how our תנא can learn from 'מטות' that a son comes first in a mother's property, yet deny that a mother inherits her son. It answers that the פסוק 'וכל בת יורשת נחלה' teaches that a woman inherits but does not pass on inheritance. A new משנה then lays out the order of heirs: son, daughter, brothers and the father's brothers. At each level, an heir's descendants take that heir's place, and a father comes before all his own descendants. The גמרא brings a ברייתא that learns this from the words 'אין לו', read as 'עיין עליו': look for descendants first.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן challenges from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן challenges רבי יהודה בן שמעון from our משנה, which says a mother does not inherit from her son.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן raised an objection to רבי יהודה בן שמעון: our משנה says that a woman with her son, a woman with her husband, and the mother's brothers all pass on inheritance but do not inherit!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן attacks רבי יהודה בן שמעון's view that a mother inherits from her son. He quotes a משנה that clearly says she does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה בן שמעון learned from the word 'מטות' that a mother inherits her son. The משנה lists 'a woman and her son' among relatives who give inheritance but never receive it. That flatly contradicts him.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection to him (usually from a משנה or ברייתא)
They pass on inheritance (to the other relative)

steps.confusionAlert: Each pair works in one direction only. The son inherits his mother, but the mother does not inherit her son. The husband inherits his wife, but the wife does not inherit her husband.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan raised an objection
to Rabbi Yehuda ben Shimon:
A woman with regard to her son,
phrases.notes: The mother passes inheritance to her son, but she doesn't inherit from him.

phrases.english: and a woman with regard to her husband,
and the mother's brothers –
pass on inheritance but do not inherit!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יהודה בן שמעון's ruling from earlier in the sugya that a mother inherits from her son.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה בן שמעון's view that a mother inherits from her son
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה explicitly lists the mother as one who passes inheritance to her son but does not inherit from him.

steps.title: I do not know who taught that משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בן שמעון answers that he does not know who authored the משנה, so he is not bound by it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: our משנה, I do not know who taught it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה בן שמעון does not answer the contradiction directly. He says the משנה has no known author, so it is not binding on him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not explain the משנה. He refuses to accept it as the final word. By saying he does not know who taught it, he treats it as an unattributed opinion that is not the accepted הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: I do not know who taught it

phrases.english: He said to him: Our mishna,
I do not know who taught it.
phrases.notes: In other words, he doesn't know any Sage who holds this, so he doesn't treat it as the final הלכה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִשְׁנָתֵנוּ, אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ מִי שְׁנָאָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוחנן's objection by rejecting the authority of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejecting the authority of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is a binding source that disproves רבי יהודה בן שמעון.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה's author is unknown, so it does not bind him.

steps.title: Why not say the משנה follows רבי זכריה בן הקצב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a better answer was not given: the משנה could simply follow רבי זכריה בן הקצב, who does not learn from 'מטות'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him say to him: it follows רבי זכריה בן הקצב, who does not learn anything from the word 'מטות'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wonders why רבי יהודה בן שמעון gave such a weak answer. He could have named a תנא who authored the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה בן שמעון's ruling depends on a derivation from 'מטות'. רבי זכריה בן הקצב does not use that derivation. So the משנה could fit רבי זכריה, and רבי יהודה בן שמעון could say he simply disagrees with that תנא.

keyTerms.meaning: But let him say to him (why not answer this way?)
A תנא quoted earlier in the פרק
Learns out (a law from a word in the פסוק)
'Tribes', the word in the פסוק used for the derivation

phrases.english: But let him say to him:
It is the opinion of Rabbi Zekharya ben HaKatzav,
who does not derive from "tribes"!
phrases.notes: Back on דף קיא, רבי זכריה didn't learn from 'מטות' that sons come before daughters in a mother's property.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵימָא לֵיהּ: רַבִּי זְכַרְיָה בֶּן הַקַּצָּב הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the answer of step 2 by offering what looks like a better answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The weak answer 'I do not know who taught it'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A known תנא, רבי זכריה בן הקצב, rejects the 'מטות' derivation. So the משנה could be attributed to him.

steps.title: The משנה says a sister's sons come first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה cannot follow רבי זכריה, because the משנה gives sisters' sons priority over sisters' daughters.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה cannot be explained as following רבי זכריה בן הקצב. It teaches 'and the sons of a sister', and a Sage taught: sons of a sister, not daughters of a sister. And we asked: for what הלכה? And רב ששת said: to come first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining why the משנה cannot be רבי זכריה's. It first lays out a detail of the same משנה: a sister's sons come before her daughters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists 'sons of a sister' among those who inherit. A ברייתא stresses that this means sons, not daughters. רב ששת explains that this does not exclude daughters entirely. It means sons inherit before them. This detail sets up the contradiction in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It cannot be explained (as following that view)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Not daughters of a sister' does not mean daughters never inherit. רב ששת explains it only means sons go first.

phrases.english: The mishna cannot be explained
in accordance with Rabbi Zekharya ben HaKatzav;
as it teaches: "And the sons of a sister,"
phrases.notes: These words are from the same משנה: a sister's sons inherit from their uncle but do not pass inheritance to him.

phrases.english: and a Sage taught: "Sons of a sister" – and not daughters of a sister.
And we said: With regard to what halakha?
And Rav Sheshet said: To precede.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא מִיתּוֹקְמָא מַתְנִיתִין כְּרַבִּי זְכַרְיָה בֶּן הַקַּצָּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering step 3 by bringing a detail of the משנה that will clash with רבי זכריה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the proposed author contradicts another part of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה could easily follow רבי זכריה בן הקצב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה gives a sister's sons priority over her daughters, which sets up a clash with רבי זכריה.

steps.title: רבי זכריה holds that son and daughter are equal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes the proof: רבי זכריה says sons and daughters share a mother's property equally, so he cannot be the author of a משנה that puts sons first.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you think the משנה follows רבי זכריה בן הקצב, doesn't he say that son and daughter are equal in the mother's property!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer. The משנה's rule that sons come first does not fit רבי זכריה, who treats sons and daughters equally in a mother's property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sister's children inherit from their uncle through their mother. That makes it a case of a mother's line. רבי זכריה holds that sons and daughters are equal in a mother's property, so he would not give the sons priority. Since the משנה does give them priority, it cannot be his. That is why רבי יהודה בן שמעון could only say 'I do not know who taught it.'
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה (mother does not inherit her son) cannot be pinned on רבי זכריה בן הקצב. The same משנה puts a sister's sons before her daughters, but רבי זכריה treats son and daughter equally in a mother's property. So רבי יהודה בן שמעון had no named תנא to point to and could only say 'I do not know who taught it.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the גמרא checks a proposed author against every part of a משנה, not only the part being discussed.

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִיתִין רַבִּי זְכַרְיָה בֶּן הַקַּצָּב הִיא,
phrases.english: that the mishna is according to Rabbi Zekharya ben HaKatzav,

phrases.aramaic: הָא אָמַר: אֶחָד הַבֵּן וְאֶחָד הַבַּת
phrases.english: doesn't he say: Both the son and the daughter
are equal with regard to the mother's property!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ מַתְנִיתִין רַבִּי זְכַרְיָה בֶּן הַקַּצָּב הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun in step 4 by showing the direct clash with רבי זכריה's view.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה cannot follow רבי זכריה בן הקצב
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי זכריה's own ruling that son and daughter are equal in a mother's property, set against the משנה's priority for a sister's sons

steps.title: Our תנא seems inconsistent either way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the תנא of our משנה: whether or not he learns from 'מטות', one of his two rulings seems to have no basis.
steps.simpleTranslation: And our תנא, whichever way you look at it, has a problem. If he learns from the word 'מטות', a woman should also inherit from her son. If he does not learn from 'מטות', where does he get the rule that a son comes before a daughter in the mother's property?
steps.whatsHappening: Having shown that the משנה is not רבי זכריה בן הקצב's view, the גמרא now asks how the משנה's own תנא can hold both of his rulings at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Comparing the mother's 'tribe' to the father's ('מטות') gives two results: a son comes before a daughter in the mother's property, and a mother inherits from her son, just as a father does. Our משנה accepts the first result but rejects the second. The גמרא asks how one source can be used for one rule but not the other.

keyTerms.meaning: The teacher of our משנה, the one who said it
Whichever way you look at it; an either-way challenge
He expounds, learns a law from a word in the פסוק

phrases.english: And our tanna, whichever way you look at it:
if he expounds the word "tribes,"
phrases.notes: This is the earlier idea of treating the mother's family line like the father's for inheritance.

phrases.english: then a woman should also inherit from her son;
if he does not expound "tribes,"

phrases.aramaic: בֵּן דְּקוֹדֵם לַבַּת בְּנִכְסֵי הָאֵם – מְנָא לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: then the rule that a son precedes a daughter in the mother's property, from where does he know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that רבי זכריה has been ruled out as the author, the גמרא challenges the internal consistency of the משנה's actual תנא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The תנא of our משנה, who gives sons priority in a mother's property but denies that a mother inherits from her son.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both rulings come from the same source ('מטות'). Accepting the source should give both rulings, and rejecting it should give neither.
steps.whyThisMatters: This forces the גמרא to show a separate source that limits the 'מטות' comparison.

steps.title: A special פסוק excludes a mother inheriting from her son
steps.stepSummary: The תנא does learn from 'מטות', but the פסוק 'וכל בת יורשת נחלה' teaches that a woman inherits and does not pass on inheritance, so a mother does not inherit from her son.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, he does learn from 'מטות'. But here it is different, because the פסוק says: 'And every daughter who inherits an inheritance.' She inherits, but she does not pass on inheritance.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the תנא accepts the 'מטות' comparison, but a specific פסוק blocks one of its results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So the son-before-daughter rule in a mother's property stands, because it comes from 'מטות'. Only the idea that a mother inherits from her son is cut off. The word 'יורשת' is read as limiting the woman's role: she receives inheritance from the tribes, but she does not pass it on to another tribe.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually; it introduces the answer that keeps the original position
She passes on an inheritance to others

steps.whatToRemember: The תנא of our משנה learns from 'מטות', which is why a son comes before a daughter even in a mother's property. A mother still does not inherit from her son, because 'יורשת ואינה מורשת' teaches she inherits but does not pass on.

phrases.english: Actually, he does expound "tribes";
but here it is different, for the verse says:
"And every daughter who inherits an inheritance"
she inherits, but she does not bequeath.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the either-way challenge of step 6 by picking the first side and limiting it with a separate פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting a general derivation with a specific פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the תנא learns from 'מטות', then every result of comparing mother to father should apply, including a mother inheriting from her son.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנא learns from 'מטות', but 'וכל בת יורשת נחלה' blocks a mother from inheriting from her son, so only the son-before-daughter rule remains.

steps.title: The order of heirs: son, daughter, brothers, uncles
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה lists the order of inheritance and teaches that each heir's descendants stand in that heir's place.
steps.simpleTranslation: The order of inheritance is like this. The פסוק says: 'If a man dies and has no son, then you shall pass his inheritance to his daughter.' So a son comes before a daughter, and all the descendants of a son come before the daughter. A daughter comes before the brothers, and a daughter's descendants come before the brothers. Brothers come before the father's brothers, and the brothers' descendants come before the father's brothers.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins, giving the basic ladder of who inherits a person's property first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order is son, then daughter, then the dead man's brothers, then his father's brothers. At every level, the descendants of a closer heir beat the next level, even if the closer heir himself has already died. For example, a son's grandchild comes before the dead man's daughter.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מתניתין, our משנה; it marks the start of a new משנה
His descendants (literally 'those who come out of his thigh')
The father's brothers, the dead man's uncles

steps.confusionAlert: 'יוצאי יריכו של בן קודמין לבת' means even a son's grandchild beats the dead man's own daughter. Closeness of the person does not decide it; the branch they come from does.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
The order of inheritances is like this:
"If a man dies and has no son,
then you shall pass his inheritance to his daughter"
so a son precedes a daughter,

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל יוֹצְאֵי יְרֵיכוֹ שֶׁל בֵּן קוֹדְמִין לַבַּת.
phrases.english: and all the descendants of a son precede the daughter.
A daughter precedes the brothers,
phrases.notes: He means the dead man's brothers.

phrases.aramaic: יוֹצְאֵי יְרֵיכָהּ שֶׁל בַּת קוֹדְמִין לָאַחִין.
phrases.english: and the descendants of a daughter precede the brothers.
Brothers precede the father's brothers,

phrases.aramaic: יוֹצְאֵי יְרֵיכָן שֶׁל אַחִין קוֹדְמִין לַאֲחֵי הָאָב.
phrases.english: and the descendants of the brothers precede the father's brothers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה begins after the previous discussion closes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Order of heirs: son (and his descendants), then daughter (and her descendants), then brothers (and their descendants), then the father's brothers.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic order of Torah inheritance that the coming discussion builds on.

steps.title: The general rule of inheritance priority
steps.stepSummary: The משנה sums up: whoever comes first in inheritance, his descendants come first too; and the father comes before all his own descendants.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the general rule: anyone who comes first in inheritance, his descendants also come first. And the father comes before all of his descendants.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes its list with a general principle that covers every level of the family.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half widens the list: any heir's descendants take that heir's place in line. The second half adds the father, who was not in the list. The dead man's father comes before everyone who descends from him, such as the dead man's brothers and their children.

keyTerms.meaning: The father (here, the dead man's father)

steps.confusionAlert: 'והאב קודם לכל יוצאי יריכו' is about the dead man's father. He comes before the dead man's brothers, because they are the father's own descendants.
steps.whatToRemember: Each heir's descendants stand in that heir's place, and a father comes before all of his own descendants.

phrases.english: This is the principle:
anyone who precedes in inheritance,
his descendants precede as well.
And the father precedes all of his descendants.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the specific examples of step 8 into a general rule and adds the father's place in line.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Descendants of a prior heir take that heir's place; the father comes before all of his own descendants.

steps.title: A son's descendants take the son's place
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the words 'אין לו' that a son's children and grandchildren come before the other relatives, just like the son himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The Sages taught: The פסוק says 'son.' From that word I would only know about a son himself. How do I know that a son's son, a son's daughter, or the son of a son's daughter also comes first? The פסוק says 'אין לו' ('he has no son'). Read it as 'עיין עליו': look into it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives the source for the משנה's rule. A son's descendants inherit in his place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק only says 'son,' which might mean the son himself and nobody else. The ברייתא reads 'אין' as 'עיין' ('look into it'). Before we skip to the daughter, we must check whether the son left any descendants. If he did, they inherit in his place.

keyTerms.meaning: I only know (this much from the פסוק)
Look into it; check whether he left descendants

steps.confusionAlert: 'עיין עליו' is not a new word in the פסוק. The ברייתא is reading the existing word 'אין' as if it said 'עיין'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the scriptural source for the משנה's principle that a descendant steps into the place of a parent who has died.

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Sages taught:
"Son" — I only know about a son himself;
a son's son, or a son's daughter,
or the son of a son's daughter, from where do we know?
The פסוק says: "he has no"
Look into it, regarding him.
phrases.notes: The ברייתא reads the word אין as if it said עיין, 'look into it': check whether the son left any descendants before moving on.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״בֵּן״ – אֵין לִי אֶלָּא בֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the scriptural source for the משנה's rule that each heir's descendants stand in that heir's place.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A son's descendants (son's son, son's daughter, son of a son's daughter) take the son's place and come before other relatives.

steps.title: A daughter's descendants take the daughter's place
steps.stepSummary: The same reading of 'אין לו' teaches that a daughter's children and grandchildren come before the brothers, just like the daughter herself.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'daughter.' From that word I would only know about a daughter herself. How do I know that a daughter's daughter, a daughter's son, or the daughter of a daughter's son also comes first? The פסוק says 'אין לו' ('he has no daughter'). Read it as 'עיין עליו': look into it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא repeats the same reading for the next פסוק. A daughter's descendants also inherit in her place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The next פסוק says that if there is no daughter, the inheritance goes to the brothers. 'אין לו' appears there too, so we must check whether the daughter left descendants. If she did, they come before the brothers.

keyTerms.meaning: The daughter of a daughter's son

steps.whatToRemember: Both the son's line and the daughter's line pass down. The words 'אין לו' tell us to look for descendants before moving to the next heir.

phrases.english: "Daughter" — I only know about a daughter herself;
a daughter's daughter, and a daughter's son,
and the daughter of a daughter's son, from where do we know?
The פסוק says: "he has no"
Look into it, regarding him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same reading of 'אין לו' from the son's פסוק to the daughter's פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A daughter's descendants (daughter's daughter, daughter's son, daughter of a daughter's son) take the daughter's place and come before the brothers.
